rfis.question_text: Reference: SLP1 - RFI0893.2 - B1 Balcony Guardrail Added Plate to Embeds Confirmation_R2 SLP1 - RFI0893.1 - B1 Balcony Guardrail Added Plate to Embeds Confirmation_R1 RFI0893.1-SK5, and SK6 Post on: Detail 8/A8.21 Background: Due to missed steel embeds at corners of Level 3 balcony curbs, the steel embeds for the balcony guardrail were set 1' off of correct locations at the SW and SE balconies. To provide an alternative means of attachment for the balcony guardrails where steel embeds are missing, we propose adding steel plates connected to the steel embeds as noted in the attached sketches. Structural confirmation for the proposed remedial solution was confirmed by Jonathan Chen of DES per response to RFI 0893.1. However, after further evaluation of the originally proposed solution it was determined that a new solution was required due to the limited space between the coping cap from the metal panel and the face of the curb. After reviewing the various options that were discussed, it was decided that the most effective solution would be to add a L5x5 angle where the 1 ½” plate cantilevers, next to the L6x7 angle that will get anchored to the side of the curb. This L5x5 would get anchored down to the SOMD and welded to the bottom of the cantilevered plate. This would occur only at the ends of the curbs where the plate is cantilevered. At the corner’s where we have a column concrete curb, we are proposing to use L5x5 angles to omit the anchor bolts at each plate. The top of the L5x5 would get welded to the bottom of the 1 ½” to provide the support needed. These angles would then get anchored down to the existing column concrete curb. Question: Q1. Please review and confirm the revised proposed sketches SK5 and SK6 (showing the addition of the steel plate per RFI 0893 and omitting the anchors) are acceptable per the attached email with Jonathan Chen/DES.
rfis.resolution_text: Please see attached.

rfis.question_text: Roof Vertical Rigid Insulation Thickness Clarification
rfis.resolution_text:
Jordan Koop (SmithGroup, Inc - 10017650): JK/SG/08.15.24 - SG recommends 1" minimum rigid insulation at 
exterior walls per details provided on PK2-A5.7.2. Exterior rigid insulation minimizes thermal bridging and 
eliminates chances of condensation within the wall.
Based off performance model updates, exterior rigid insulation is not required to achieve net zero EUI and Title 
24 requirements if 6" batt insulation is provided within the wall assembly. Please note that 6" of batt insulation 
does not achieve R-19 due to thermal bridging.
Nisha Dev (DPR Construction): Copy pasted from email - JK/SG/08.22.24 - We recommend 3" rigid insulation at the 
exterior. Per direction from DPR we explored reducing exterior insulation.

rfis.question_text: Ref: Spec Section 114000, pg 75-79 (Item R1000 - Remote Refrigeration Package): Sections E & F call out for monitoring systems such that "Control system shall be interconnected to the local area network and be capable of sending alarm alerts via mobile telephone or e-mail." This RFI is requesting clarification for two items: 1. There are (2) means of monitoring the units- please advise if Option A or Option B is preferred. Note that the evaporator coil is located on the roof. Option A: BMS Integration (recommended) - Integration Card (ilC) gets procured & installed at the evaporator coil controller board. Controls team would tie into the integration card & back to the BMS to allow for monitoring via the BMS system. Option B: Typical Internet/Router-Based - Webserver Card (iWC) gets procured & installed at the evaporator coil controller board. WBE would need to add low voltage drop (or router location would need to be able to use an existing free data port adjacent to the walk-ins). Property Management would need to procure a router, which would plug in to an ethernet port at the card & the wall to allow for monitoring. This would likely also require making a little weather enclosure for the router/cabling to avoid weather damage. 2. Spec section 114000 does not appear to specify exactly what conditions alarms should be sent for, and what the preferred method of alarm is (text versus email versus both). Please provide a list of alarm criteria (eg temperature is above setpoint by x degrees for more than 15 minutes or similar)
rfis.resolution_text: Julia Morini (DES Architects & Engineers, Inc. - 10012655): Please see attached.

rfis.question_text: The bolt passing through the holes in the beam needs to be centered to allow for the minimum required 1 1/2" wood plugs on both sides. Currently, when we tighten the nut, the bolt is off-center, which prevents the 1 1/2" plug from fitting on one side. Suggested answer The above RFI solution has already been confirmed acceptable by GPLA; RFI for record to capture formally.
rfis.resolution_text:
Armando Messina (GPLA Structural Engineers): Confirmed. Please make sure to also use a washer with the nut on 
the threaded side of the bolt. Please note that the specific dimensions noted in this RFI were discussed and 
coordinated for 7 1/2" long bolts going into 10 3/4" beams. For different bolt lengths and/or beam widths, the 
amount of washer buildup required may be different. In any case, all bolts should have at least (1) washer on each 
side of the connection.

rfis.question_text: Ref: Attached RFI markup; GLT panels over the wedge area are not sitting flush over wedge steel (i.e. there are various gaps between top of steel and bottom of panel). Given as built information, please provide structural solution to get wedge steel and GLT panels in alignment and to intended elevation.
rfis.resolution_text:
Armando Messina (GPLA Structural Engineers): The field measurements provided indicate that the W18x46 beam 
running along GL-A is at a different slope from the rest of the wedge, with its north end protruding above the 
plane of the wedge. This is pushing the GLT panels upwards and not allowing them to sit flush with the rest of the 
wedge steel. The proposed solution is to lower the north end of that beam so that it aligns with the rest of the 
wedge plane and the panels can sit flush. Please see attached SSK-RFI-263 for a proposed sequence to achieve 
this and connection details for re-attaching the beam to the structure.

rfis.question_text: South CMU Wall of Electrical Room 503 is exposed on back side to Ramp from Tier 5 to Tier 6. Wind driven rain hits the wall, and is able to saturate through CMU blocks, seeping into inside of electrical room. Per drawings, no sealer is currently installed at CMU. Per input from Sherwin Williams Representative, suggested solution is: Prime with - Loxon Masonry Primer 2 Coats - Loxon XP Waterproofing Masonry Coating.
